ci-bot: PERFORMANCE CI /pr/6905 failed: microbench/kv_hit_rate_latency diff +12.3% (> +5% threshold). logs: https://ci.redwood/example/6905/artifacts :warning:

sam: ugh, saw this when I merged the batching heuristic tweak earlier today. PR is 6905 (batch heuristics + kernel hints).
sam: failing test is `microbench/kv_hit_rate_latency` on A100-80GB, seq_len=32 workload.
maria: can you paste the CI artifact perf summary? :eyes:

sam: summary from artifact:
```
baseline mean_latency_ms: 18.2
post-merge mean_latency_ms: 20.4
delta: +12.09%
kv_hit_rate baseline: 74.1% -> post: 68.3% (drop)
kernel_selected: cuBLAS->custom_matmul_heuristic_v2
```

jordan: interesting — kernel change + kv hit drop. sounds like the new batching window is causing more partial batches which prevents kv cache reuse.

alex: i added a small change to kernel hinting in 3f5a7b1 (PR 6898) to prefer smaller matmul kernels for short sequences. might be related.

maria: can we bisect quickly across the last 3 merges?
jordan: running `git bisect` against main with the perf job locally now, will ping when I have the commit.

perf-bot: bisect started by jordan. Job: microbench/kv_hit_rate_latency seq=32 on A100.

jordan: bisect result: culprit range narrowed to commit 3f5a7b1 -> 8b2c9d4. First bad commit: 3f5a7b1 (alex) — kernel hint change.

sam: that matches my mental model. Alex's hint probably pushes requests to `custom_matmul_heuristic_v2` which has slightly different padding behavior and prevents kv prefix matching on our builder.

lin: quick check of kernel selector logs from the CI run (trimmed):
```
[kernel_selector] seq=32 batch=1 pref=small_kernel
selected: custom_matmul_heuristic_v2
kv_cache_key: generated_for_prefix_len=0
cache_lookup: miss -> reason: partial_batch_padding_mismatch
```

alex: confirmed I changed preference ordering but didn't account for our batch padding compatibility. Sorry, my bad.

maria: what's the risk of reverting 3f5a7b1? any other regressions?

jordan: revert would restore prior kernel selection and kv hit rate, CI should be green. No other functional changes — it's a perf-only hint.
sam: can we instead patch selector to fallback to pad-compatible kernel when kv prefix reuse detected? might be smaller blast radius than revert.

lin: patch idea (pseudo):
```
if kv_prefix_detected and selected_kernel.padding_incompatible:
  fallback = find_compatible_kernel()
  selected = fallback
```

alex: i can ship a tiny fix PR that adds that check + unit test for padding compatibility. but it needs quick CI run.
maria: we have a rollout scheduled; can't carry this regression. We should revert to unblock and then merge alex's fix.

sam: agreed. Please open revert PR and label it `rollout-blocker`. I'll approve.

alex: opened PR 6906 revert of 3f5a7b1 — https://git.redwood/pr/6906 :rocket:
ci-bot: PR 6906 opened, running inbound CI (microbench smoke + unit tests).

jordan: once revert CI passes, i'll re-run the perf ci to validate kv hit back to baseline.

perf-bot: perf run queued: microbench/kv_hit_rate_latency seq=32 on A100. Artifact: https://ci.redwood/example/6906/perf

maria: nice work bisecting quickly. after revert, alex please add the pad-compat fallback and a microbench that asserts kv_hit_rate doesn't drop >2%.

alex: will do, thanks for quick turnaround. :pray:

sam: note for postmortem: kernel-hint changes need a perf checklist: kv cache compatibility, padding semantics, and microbench smoke against seq<=64.

lin: adding checklist to the PR template and a `perf-smoke` gate job.

ci-bot: PR 6906 CI passed. merge queued.

sam: merged revert. rollout unblocked. thanks everyone. :tada:

jordan: follow-up issue created: #3125 "kernel hint padding compatibility + kv-cache safety" assigned to alex.

alex: taking it. will include unit tests and a microbench assertion.

perf-bot: thread summary: revert merged to fix +12% latency on microbench; follow-up fix PR incoming.
